restatements.text: Establishes the measure's title as the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act.
Provides the short title for the measure.
Details findings regarding threats of funding cuts to health care, public education, and food programs, and argues that taxing billionaires' wealth is an equitable way to backfill these cuts.
Outlines the measure's purpose to raise revenue through a one-time wealth tax to support health care, education, and nutrition programs.

Authorizes a one-time tax on the personal property and wealth of California billionaires, establishes the Reserve Fund separate from the General Fund, and directs 90% of revenue to a Health Account and 10% to an Education and Food Assistance Account.

Specifies how the Health and Education/Food Assistance Accounts may be used, authorizes legislative appropriations up to certain caps, mandates that funds cannot supplant existing state spending, requires the Department of Finance to report annually on the fund's status, and authorizes a start-up loan for the Franchise Tax Board.
Creates the title for the new tax code part.

Imposes a 5% excise tax on the net worth of California residents and applicable trusts with a net worth of $1 billion or more for the 2026 tax year, and outlines filing options and Franchise Tax Board audit powers.
Defines how debts and liabilities are taken into account when calculating a taxpayer's net worth, including limitations on related-party and contingent debts.

Establishes valuation methods for different types of assets, exempts directly-held real property and certain retirement accounts, and mandates certified appraisals for non-public assets over $1 million.
Creates Optional Deferral Accounts (ODA) to allow certain taxpayers with liquidity constraints to defer paying the tax until material distributions or withdrawals are made.
Requires appraisers making certified appraisals to follow specific rules and allows the Board to penalize appraisers for substantial overstatements or understatements of valuation.
Provides rules for apportioning the tax if the taxpayer claims the accumulated wealth was not substantially sustained in California, placing the burden of proof on the petitioning party.
Allows a pro rata credit against the tax for net wealth taxes paid to other jurisdictions.
Defines key terms for the administration of the tax, including 'applicable individual', 'grantor trust', 'net worth', and the specific dates for tax obligations and valuations.
Grants the Franchise Tax Board authority to adopt regulations to administer the tax, exempts these regulations from the Administrative Procedure Act until 2028, and sets forms and filing provisions.
Permits the Legislature to amend the statutory provisions by a two-thirds vote if the changes further the measure's purposes.
Provides that the provisions of the Act are severable and instructs courts to adjust dates rather than invalidate the tax if constitutional defects are found.
Imposes penalties of 20% or 40% for substantial or gross understatements of tax, and grants the Board broad power to disregard transactions lacking economic substance.
Instructs that the provisions of the tax code be liberally construed to effectuate their purposes.
Establishes expedited judicial review procedures for facial challenges to the Act's validity.
Disallows a deduction under the state income tax for the wealth tax imposed by this measure.
Specifies that this measure will supersede any conflicting billionaire wealth tax measure on the same ballot if it receives more votes.
Authorizes the measure's proponents or any citizen to defend its legality in court if the state does not.

evidence.quote: Notwithstanding Section 32 or any other provision of law, a facial challenge to the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act is authorized to be adjudicated through a validation action under Chapter 6 of Part 27 of the Revenue and Taxation Code, Section 50314 without requiring the payment of the tax claimed to be facially invalid.
evidence.why: It strengthens due process by allowing taxpayers to challenge the tax in court without having to pay the tax upfront first.

evidence.quote: For all other interests in any business entities including all equity and other ownership interests, all debt interests, and all other contractual or noncontractual interests, the fair market value of those interests at the end of any tax year shall be presumed to be the sum of the book value of the business entity according to generally accepted accounting principles as of the end of the tax year plus a present-value multiplier of 7.5 times the annual book profits of the business entity-as averaged over the current tax year and the preceding two tax years, if available-according to generally accepted accounting principles, with this entire sum then multiplied by the percentage of the business entity owned by the taxpayer as of the end of the tax year.
evidence.why: It increases the complexity of tax rules by requiring the use of specific formulas and multipliers to value non-publicly traded business interests.

evidence.quote: An excise tax is imposed for tax year 2026 on the activity of sustaining excessive accumulations of wealth by applicable individuals with net worth of $1 billion dollars ($1,000,000,000) or more, and on applicable trusts.
evidence.why: It levies a new 5% wealth tax exclusively on individuals possessing at least $1 billion, increasing the share of taxes paid by the highest wealth brackets.

evidence.quote: With the exception of assets so excluded, a taxpayer must report the fair market value of those assets, and for each asset or group of substantially interchangeable assets (such as derivative contracts relating to the same underlying security) worth in excess of $1 million ($1,000,000), the taxpayer shall submit a certified appraisal.
evidence.why: It requires individuals to compile and report detailed valuations of their personal property and non-public assets to the state government.

evidence.quote: If the Board determines that a transaction or series of transactions lack economic substance, or that a substantial purpose for any transaction or series of transactions was to obtain a tax benefit with respect to this Part that is not intended by the voters or the Legislature, the Board may determine the tax consequences to any person in a manner that is reasonable in light of all the facts and circumstances in order to deny such benefit.
evidence.why: It expands the power of the Franchise Tax Board, allowing it to unilaterally disregard transactions and alter tax consequences if it deems they lack economic substance.

evidence.quote: Ninety percent shall be allocated to the Billionaire Tax Health Account for health care funding, which may include expenditures to restore or address any reductions in federal funding or state appropriations; investments to protect or enhance Medi-Cal and other health coverage programs for low-and moderate-income individuals; support for safety net health care providers serving vulnerable populations
evidence.why: It explicitly directs revenue to protect Medi-Cal and fund safety net clinics, which expands or protects access to healthcare for low-income populations.

evidence.quote: With the exception of assets so excluded, a taxpayer must report the fair market value of those assets, and for each asset or group of substantially interchangeable assets (such as derivative contracts relating to the same underlying security) worth in excess of $1 million ($1,000,000), the taxpayer shall submit a certified appraisal.
evidence.why: It imposes significant new reporting and compliance burdens on individuals to obtain certified appraisals for non-publicly traded assets and complex financial instruments.

evidence.quote: If the Board determines that a transaction or series of transactions lack economic substance, or that a substantial purpose for any transaction or series of transactions was to obtain a tax benefit with respect to this Part that is not intended by the voters or the Legislature, the Board may determine the tax consequences to any person in a manner that is reasonable in light of all the facts and circumstances in order to deny such benefit.
evidence.why: It delegates substantial discretionary authority to the appointed Franchise Tax Board to interpret intent and deny tax benefits based on its assessment of economic substance.

evidence.quote: the Department of Finance, in consultation with relevant state agencies, shall provide to the Legislature all the following information: (1) The current balance in the Reserve Fund as of the reporting date; (2) The estimated revenue to be generated... (4) Proposed expenditures from the Reserve Fund... (7) A certification that moneys from the Reserve Fund are not being used to supplant or replace state funding that would otherwise be appropriated.
evidence.why: It requires the state to issue detailed annual reports tracking the balances, spending, and revenues of the new fund, strengthening public oversight.

evidence.quote: After accounting for administrative expenses as provided by law, the Controller shall allocate and transfer the remaining moneys in the Reserve Fund to the following sub-accounts, which are hereby created: 90% to the Billionaire Tax Health Account and 10% to the Billionaire Tax Education and Food Assistance Account.
evidence.why: It earmarks all tax revenue specifically for health care, education, and food assistance accounts.

evidence.quote: Notwithstanding any other law, the Reserve Fund is a special fund, permanently separate and apart from the General Fund or any other state fund or account. The taxes and the moneys resulting from the Act shall not be considered to be part of the General Fund
evidence.why: It locks the generated revenue out of the General Fund, permanently restricting it to specific health, education, and nutrition purposes.

evidence.quote: If the Board determines that a transaction or series of transactions lack economic substance, or that a substantial purpose for any transaction or series of transactions was to obtain a tax benefit with respect to this Part that is not intended by the voters or the Legislature, the Board may determine the tax consequences to any person in a manner that is reasonable in light of all the facts and circumstances in order to deny such benefit.
evidence.why: It places discretionary power to rule on the economic substance of transactions and to adjust tax consequences with the appointed members of the Franchise Tax Board.

evidence.quote: Ten percent shall be allocated to the Billionaire Tax Education and Food Assistance Account for education-related and food assistance expenditures, which may include: (A) Education-related expenditures to restore or address any reductions in federal funding or state appropriations, or to make investments to protect or enhance the kindergarten through grade fourteen public education system.
evidence.why: It provides dedicated funding intended to restore cuts and stabilize resources for K-14 public schools.

evidence.quote: The penalty for a substantial understatement under this Section shall be an amount equal to 20 percent of any understatement of tax.
evidence.why: It exposes taxpayers to significant new financial penalties if their wealth valuations are found to understate their actual tax liability.

evidence.quote: The penalty for a substantial understatement under this Section shall be an amount equal to 20 percent of any understatement of tax.
evidence.why: It creates heavy new penalties allowing the state to penalize those who improperly value their wealth.

evidence.quote: After accounting for administrative expenses as provided by law, the Controller shall allocate and transfer the remaining moneys in the Reserve Fund to the following sub-accounts, which are hereby created: 90% to the Billionaire Tax Health Account and 10% to the Billionaire Tax Education and Food Assistance Account.
evidence.why: It channels the tax revenue directly into funding public health, education, and food programs.

evidence.quote: If the Board determines that a transaction or series of transactions lack economic substance, or that a substantial purpose for any transaction or series of transactions was to obtain a tax benefit with respect to this Part that is not intended by the voters or the Legislature, the Board may determine the tax consequences to any person in a manner that is reasonable in light of all the facts and circumstances in order to deny such benefit.
evidence.why: It broadens the regulatory authority of the state tax agency, allowing it to actively deny tax benefits by determining the economic substance of transactions.

evidence.quote: An excise tax is imposed for tax year 2026 on the activity of sustaining excessive accumulations of wealth by applicable individuals with net worth of $1 billion dollars ($1,000,000,000) or more, and on applicable trusts.
evidence.why: It significantly increases taxes for individuals whose wealth meets the $1 billion threshold.

evidence.quote: An excise tax is imposed for tax year 2026 on the activity of sustaining excessive accumulations of wealth by applicable individuals with net worth of $1 billion dollars ($1,000,000,000) or more, and on applicable trusts.
evidence.why: It subjects individuals with a net worth over $1 billion to a unique wealth tax not applied to other income brackets, increasing disparity in tax rates across income and wealth classes.

evidence.quote: Until January 1, 2028, the rulemaking provisions of the Administrative Procedure Act (Chapter 3.5 (commencing with Section 11340) of Part 1 of Division 3 of Title 2 of the Government Code) shall not apply to any regulation, standard, criterion, procedure, determination, rule, notice, guideline, or any other guidance established or issued by the Board pursuant to this Part.
evidence.why: It exempts the Franchise Tax Board from the standard procedural oversight of the Administrative Procedure Act, reducing the usual checks on executive rulemaking.

evidence.quote: All interests in any real property held directly by a taxpayer or held via a revocable trust shall not be included in net worth.
evidence.why: It provides a specific exemption for direct investments in real property, sheltering that particular asset class from the wealth tax.

analysis.answer: Current law was not provided. The measure creates a one-time 5% excise tax on the total net worth of California residents who hold $1 billion or more in wealth as of January 1, 2026. Revenues are placed in a new Reserve Fund strictly designated for health care, education, and food assistance, bypassing the state's General Fund.

The state faces direct costs to fund the Franchise Tax Board (which is granted up to $50 million as a start-up loan) to process complex business appraisals, audit returns, and manage litigation. Taxpayers will bear substantial compliance costs hiring certified appraisers and accountants to determine the value of non-public assets, trusts, and complex holdings.

California residents with a net worth over $1 billion will pay the tax, though those whose wealth is primarily in directly held real estate are largely exempted. The practical beneficiaries are lower-income Californians relying on Medi-Cal and CalFresh, public school districts, and safety-net health clinics. Appraisers and tax attorneys will also see increased business.

Billionaires may attempt to alter their legal residency before the tax obligation date, restructure assets to exploit the real-estate exemption, or file lawsuits to delay or invalidate the tax. Taxpayers without sufficient liquid cash may utilize the Optional Deferral Accounts. The state tax board will likely rapidly expand its auditing staff and promulgate broad anti-avoidance rules.

The measure addresses projected shortfalls in Medi-Cal, public schools, and food assistance caused by state and federal budget cuts, while noting that billionaires pay low effective tax rates because their wealth grows untaxed. The mechanism—a one-time 5% direct tax on net worth—aims to capture this un realized wealth to backfill safety net programs.

The Franchise Tax Board gains extraordinary discretion to rewrite the tax consequences of financial transactions if it determines they lack 'economic substance', and is permitted to do so without the normal constraints of the Administrative Procedure Act until 2028.

Researchers disagree on the effectiveness of state-level wealth taxes. Some studies find they are an efficient way to capture untaxed economic gains from the ultra-wealthy and raise substantial revenue for public needs. Other researchers find wealth taxes are highly volatile, difficult to enforce due to valuation challenges and capital mobility, and can result in out-migration of high-net-worth individuals, which may ultimately depress overall state income tax collections.

A substantial sum will be absorbed by administrative and legal costs. The complex valuation formulas for private equity and closely held businesses guarantee significant expenditures on audits and lengthy litigation over valuations and anti-avoidance rules, though it is a small fraction of the billions in revenue projected.

Because the tax is fundamentally authorized by a constitutional amendment, repealing the tax authority would require another vote of the people. The Legislature may amend the statutory machinery by a two-thirds vote, but only if the amendments are consistent with and further the measure's original purposes.

flags.quote: Notwithstanding any other law, the Reserve Fund is a special fund, permanently separate and apart from the General Fund or any other state fund or account.
The Board shall have the authority to adopt regulations to implement, interpret, make specific, or otherwise carry out any provision of this Part.
flags.note: The administration of the tax heavily depends on regulations issued by the FTB.

flags.quote: The provisions of the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act, also referred to as "the Act," are severable.
flags.note: Contains a severability clause, including specific instructions to courts to adjust dates rather than strike down the tax if it is found constitutionally defective.
Sets a clear and rapid effective date for tax liability.

flags.quote: The Legislature may amend the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act, by statute passed in each house of the Legislature by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring, if the statute is consistent with and furthers the purposes of the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act.
flags.note: Imposes supermajority requirements and 'furthers the purposes' limits on legislative amendments.
